To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) Tourism is a robust predictor of higher than average growth rates.

(a) tourism is associated with higher per-capita GDP growth rates than non-tourism countries, (b) this positive effect is robust and statistically significant, (c) this effect is independent from the presence of good institutions, and (d) tourism is not a substitute for good institutions.

(i) tourism is positively associated with economic growth; (ii) this result holds after controlling for a variety of institutional and geographical variables; and (iii) the positive impact of tourism on growth is not due to reverse causality.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between tourism and economic growth.
the question of whether the positive effect of tourism on growth is in fact driven by good institutions, or whether it is a robust phenomenon in itself.
the role of tourism in economic growth.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
tourism is a growth enhancing factor, but that this is not a general rule and that the presence of good institutions is a necessary condition.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
tourism is a robust determinant of growth and that the positive impact of tourism is not driven by the presence or absence of institutions.

tourism is not a panacea but it is a good medicine for lagging countries.

tourism is a robust predictor of economic growth, even when we control for the quality of institutions.
